newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran raises minimum wage by about 23 percent.
newsitem.headline: Iran raises minimum wage by about 23 percent.

text.p: Iran is raising its minimum wage by almost 23 percent, Tehran radio said on Monday.

It quoted Deputy Labour and Social Affairs Minister Mohsen Khajenouri as saying the minimum daily wage would be 8,482 rials from the start of the Iranian new year on March 21 -- 22.8 percent higher than the current 6,907 rials.
The new minimum wage is equal to $2.83 at the official exchange rate.

Faced with an official annual inflation rate of about 25 percent, Iran tries to keep basic goods at a affordable prices for low-income groups by subsidising them. The budget for the next year includes $1.4 billion earmarked for food subsidies.
A senior Iranian official said in June that people earning less than 680,000 rials a month in Tehran were beneath the poverty line.
($1 = 3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
